newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Griffin oilfield resumes after tropical storm.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Griffin oilfield resumes after tropical storm.

text.p: Oil production from the Griffin field off the coast of Western Australia resumed at 7.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) after an 18 hour shutdown due to bad weather from a tropical low, a spokesman for BHP Petroleum Pty Ltd.
The spokesman for the unit of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said the field was shut-in at 1.30 p.m. (0530 GMT) on Wednesday.
He said one vessel was loaded before the halt but could not quantify lost production. Griffin produces about 80,000 barrels per day.
BHP has a 45 percent stake in Griffin and is the operator, followed by Mobil Corp with 35 percent and Inpex Alpha Ltd with 20 percent.
Cossack produces about 65,000 barrels per day and is owned by the North West Shelf partners, which includes the operator Woodside with an equal one-sixth stake.

The other five partners are BHP, British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd -- a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp -- Chevron Corp, and Royal Dutch/Shell Group. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
